Built around your say-so

More capability.

Agents need room to be useful. You need to understand what they can access and what they are doing.

Fuego’s approach is explicit: scoped access, visible activity, and a way to pause and review. Your workspace should make that control easier to use.

A few things to know

Before the
next spark.

Can I use Fuego today?+

Fuego is in active development, with a working internal deployment and focused testing across its Mac and cloud workflows. There is no general public download or self-service signup yet. This site is a look at the product and its direction.

Is Fuego another AI model?+

Fuego is a workspace for coordinating AI agents and the resources they use. It is designed to bring your choice of supported AI services, accounts, and connected computers into a shared place for work. Provider support is being qualified individually.

Does everything run on my computer?+

Fuego combines a central workspace with connected execution computers. Where a task runs and which AI service processes it depend on the setup. Connected computers do not imply that every model or every part of the system runs locally.

Do I need NeroNook?+

No. Fuego has its own workspace. NeroNook is an optional Mac companion that can keep Fuego work close alongside your other everyday tools. The two products can be used independently.

What’s next?+

The focus is dependable everyday work: smoother setup, clearer account and computer management, and better continuity between Fuego and NeroNook. Broader platform support and a public release remain in development.
